tour.name: Palenque Private Tour: the Maya City in the Jungle, Misol-Ha & Agua Azul Waterfalls
tour.subtitle: The most atmospheric Maya city in a private day with a licensed guide and vehicle: the Temple of the Inscriptions and the tomb of King Pakal, the Palace and its tower, jungle trails to hidden temples with howler monkeys, and swims at the Misol-Ha and Agua Azul waterfalls.

tour.overview:
Palenque, in the rainforest of Chiapas, was a powerful Maya city that reached its height in the 7th century under King K'inich Janaab Pakal. Its temples, palaces and inscriptions are among the finest of Maya art. In 1952, the archaeologist Alberto Ruz discovered Pakal's tomb deep inside the Temple of the Inscriptions, with its carved sarcophagus lid and jade mask. It has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1987.

This private day takes you through the ruins and the jungle with a licensed guide and a vehicle, followed by two of the most beautiful waterfalls in Mexico.

AT A GLANCE
• Duration: about 10 hours
• Start and end: your hotel in Palenque
• Type: private tour with licensed guide, vehicle and driver
• Booking: on request – we confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay only then
• Level: moderate; jungle trails and steps

WHAT YOU SEE
• Palenque ruins.
• Jungle trails.
• The site museum.
• Misol-Ha.
• Agua Azul.

WHY THIS WORKS
An early start brings you to the ruins in the cool morning mist, and the vehicle links the waterfalls in the afternoon.

WHO IT SUITS
History lovers, nature lovers and photographers.

WHO MAY PREFER ANOTHER TOUR
To continue to San Cristóbal de las Casas, ask us for a one-way version.

PRACTICAL INFORMATION
Agua Azul is turquoise mainly in the dry season (about February to May); after rain it turns brown. Bring insect repellent.

days.name: The ruins of Palenque, the jungle, Misol-Ha and Agua Azul
days.description:
What to expect: the Maya city in the rainforest and two waterfalls, with a licensed guide, private vehicle, entrances and lunch.

Your guide and driver collect you at about 7:30 and drive to the ruins, arriving at opening time, when mist often drifts through the trees and howler monkeys roar. You see the Temple of the Inscriptions, whose hieroglyphic panels tell the history of the city, and learn about the discovery of Pakal's tomb. In the Palace, a complex of courtyards and galleries, you see the carved stucco reliefs and the four-storey tower. Across the stream, the temples of the Cross Group, of the Sun, the Cross and the Foliated Cross, have carved panels inside. A trail leads down through the jungle past waterfalls and smaller ruins to the museum, where you see the replica of Pakal's sarcophagus lid and incense burners.

After lunch, you drive to Misol-Ha, where a waterfall drops about 35 metres into a pool; a path leads behind the curtain of water. You continue to Agua Azul, a series of cascades and turquoise pools in the forest, where you can swim in the safe areas, before returning to Palenque.

SCHEDULE (approximate times)
07:30 – Pick-up.
08:00 – Palenque ruins.
11:00 – Jungle trail and museum.
12:30 – Lunch.
14:00 – Misol-Ha.
15:30 – Agua Azul.
18:30 – Back at your hotel.

GOOD TO KNOW
• Swim only in the marked areas at Agua Azul.
• The Bonampak and Yaxchilán ruins can be visited on a separate day.

INCLUDED: private vehicle and driver, licensed guide, entrances, lunch, bottled water, hotel pick-up and drop-off.
NOT INCLUDED: drinks, tips.

Overnight: none.
Meals: lunch.

faq.question: How does booking on request work?
faq.answer: You choose a date and the number of travellers and send the request. Nothing is charged. We confirm availability and the final price by email within 24 hours, and you pay online only when the tour is confirmed.

faq.question: Can we see Pakal’s tomb?
faq.answer: The tomb itself is closed to protect it; the museum has a replica of the lid and the jade mask is in Mexico City.

faq.question: Can we swim at the waterfalls?
When is Agua Azul turquoise?
faq.answer: In the dry season, about February to May.

faq.question: Is it suitable for children?
faq.answer: Yes, for children who enjoy walking and swimming.

faq.question: Is it suitable for people with limited mobility?
faq.answer: Partly. The main plaza is accessible; jungle trails have steps.

faq.question: Is Chiapas safe for visitors?
faq.answer: The tourist route is generally safe; we monitor conditions and adapt if needed.

faq.question: Will we be taken to shops?
faq.answer: No. There are no commission stops.

faq.question: What should we wear?
faq.answer: Light clothes, walking shoes, swimwear and insect repellent.

faq.question: What is the best time of year?
Should we tip?
faq.answer: Tipping is customary in Mexico: 10 to 15 percent for guides and drivers is usual if you were happy with the service, but it is always your choice.

faq.question: What is the cancellation policy?
faq.answer: You can cancel free of charge up to 24 hours before the tour. Until your request is confirmed, nothing is charged at all.
